title: Defining Basic Mixins with @mixin
ques: Explain the role of **mixins** in Sass. Write a basic mixin named `flex-center` that centers content along both axes and include it in a container.
explanation: Mixins encapsulate reusable blocks of CSS declarations. The `@mixin` directive defines the bundle, and the `@include` directive injects it into selectors.

title: Passing Arguments to Mixins
ques: Write a mixin named `square` that accepts a `size` parameter and sets both `width` and `height` properties.
explanation: Parameters allow mixins to dynamically calculate or assign property values for different use cases.

title: Configuring Default Arguments
ques: Write a `box-shadow-custom` mixin with **default argument values** for horizontal offset, vertical offset, blur radius, spread, and color.
explanation: Default arguments (`$param: defaultValue`) provide standard fallback values so callers only need to supply arguments when overriding defaults.

title: Using Keyword Arguments
ques: Demonstrate the use of **Keyword Arguments** when invoking a mixin to skip intermediate default parameters.
explanation: Keyword arguments (`@include mixin($paramName: value)`) make code self-documenting and let developers pass parameters out of order or skip defaults.

title: Passing Content Blocks with @content
ques: Explain the **`@content`** directive. Write a responsive breakpoint mixin `for-tablet` that wraps passed style blocks within a `@media` query.
explanation: The `@content` directive acts as a slot inside a mixin where entire nested rulesets or property blocks passed by callers are injected.

title: Custom Sass Functions with @function and @return
ques: Explain how a **Sass function** differs from a mixin. Write a custom function `rem-calc($px-value)` that converts pixel values into `rem` units based on a 16px root size.
explanation: Mixins output CSS property blocks and selectors, whereas `@function` computations take inputs and return a single scalar value using `@return`.
